name: Tsakonian

ancestors.notes: Only living descendant of Doric Greek (likely of Laconic Doric), not of Attic-Ionic/Koine like every other modern Greek variety (Wikipedia: Tsakonian language; Wikipedia: Doric Greek).

notes: Tsakonian (Τσακωνικά), spoken around Mount Parnon in the eastern Peloponnese (Leonidio, Tyros, Prastos, Kastanitsa). Uses the standard Greek alphabet plus digraphs for sounds absent from, or uncommon in, Demotic Greek: ⟨σχ⟩=[ʃ] (like German ‘sch’), ⟨τσχ⟩=[tʃ], ⟨τθ κχ πφ⟩=aspirated stops [tʰ kʰ pʰ], ⟨ρζ⟩=[ʒ] (corrected from an earlier draft's [rʒ] after checking the Wikipedia transcription table, which gives ρζ as the voiced postalveolar fricative alone, not a cluster). Most of these digraphs are not the concatenation of their parts under the standard Greek reading (σ+χ would give [sx], not [ʃ]) so they earn grapheme keys of their own under AGENTS.md §2 test 1. ⟨τσχ⟩ is the one exception where the surface IPA happens to equal the concatenation of ⟨τ⟩=[t] and the already-registered ⟨σχ⟩=[ʃ]; its key is still legitimate under §2 test 2 because [tʃ] is a single affricate segment, not a consonant cluster — the same rationale AGENTS.md gives for ⟨dž⟩/⟨ts⟩. Costakis also devised a diacritic-based alternative orthography, not modelled here. Base Greek-letter inventory inherited from Modern Greek (`el`) since Tsakonian orthography otherwise follows the standard Greek alphabet; this is a spelling-convenience inheritance only — Tsakonian's genetic ancestry is Doric, not the Attic-Ionic/Koine line `el` descends from, so `parent`/`ancestors` route through the Doric Greek clade instead of `el` or `grc`. Not independently verified against a phonology monograph (e.g. Costakis 1951) beyond the cited Wikipedia summary; quality kept at `skeleton` pending a primary-source pass.

location.notes: Tsakonia region, eastern Peloponnese, around Mount Parnon (Leonidio/Tyros area).
